Beállítom Navracsics Tibor korábbi közigazgatási és területfejlesztési miniszter augusztus 20-án bejelentette, hogy társadalmi kezdeményezést indít a „polgári demokraták” nevében . A videóban a volt miniszter mellett felbukkant Ferencz Orsolya egykori űrbiztos, a Fidesz volt országgyűlési képviselője is. Péntek este elindult a Polgári Demokraták nevű Facebook-oldal , a 444 pedig azt is észrevette, hogy június 17-én valakik bejegyeztek egy weboldalt polgaridemokratak.hu címen, amin egyelőre még nincs tartalom . A Facebook-oldalra Navracsics bejelentését és pénteki ATV-s interjúját töltötték fel, cikkünk megjelenése után arról is posztoltak, hogy Porga Gyula, Veszprém polgármestere csatlakozott a kezdeményezéshez. Egyébként ez lesz a Polgári Demokraták hivatalos oldala, mert Navracsics Tibor , majd Ferencz Orsolya is megosztotta azt a Facebookján. Navracsics a csütörtöki videójában arról beszélt, hogy „két oldal helyett egyenes út kell”, mert Magyarország eljutott abba a helyzetbe, amikor „két oldal végletes, végzetes szembenállása az ország egységét rombolja, cselekvőképességét rontja”. Szerinte ezért párbeszédre van szükség, ami felülírja a két oldal szembenállását. Ígérete szerint párthovatartozástól függetlenül mindenkit hív, hogy beszélgessen az ország jövőjéről és az elmúlt 100 nap, 16 és 36 év tanulságairól. Hogy Navracsics pontosan milyen platformon képzeli el a párbeszédet, nem derült ki, mint ahogy az sem, kikkel képzeli el az „egyenes út” építését. A videóban feltűnő Ferencz Orsolya nemrég arról beszélt, a kormányoldal elmulasztotta az érdemi megújulást . Az erről szóló bejegyzést Navracsics is megosztotta, azzal a kommentárral, hogy „Ferencz Orsolya most is pontosan fogalmazott”. Navracsics egy hónappal ezelőtt a Telexnek arról beszélt Tusványoson , hogy rendszeresen beszélget Orbán Viktorral, és azt reméli, van lehetősége befolyásolni a Fidesz irányát, viszont úgy látja, hogy a megújulás csak a pártot évtizedek óta irányító Orbánnal lehetséges. Cikkünk frissült a Polgári Demokraták Facebookján közzétett új poszttal, és azzal, hogy ez lesz a kezdeményezés hivatalos oldala. Kedvenceink Partnereinktől Állítsd be a Telexet megbízható forrásnak! https://www.thejc.com/news/israel/israel.text: Please refresh the page for the latest updates. All times are GMT. 5pm – Thank you for following the JC’s live blog We will be pausing our coverage as no result is expected imminently. Visit our election hub to follow the final vote tallies as they come in. And while we wait, why not read Stephen Pollard’s analysis of an eventful election night – Echoes of Brexit as pundits called it wrong in writing off Bibi prematurely 4.46pm – CEC reviewing Likud claims of voter fraud “The Central Elections Committee has launched its election-integrity monitoring operation, as it does in every election, as part of which all inquiries from parties concerning election integrity or alleged errors in the results will be examined,” the committee said. “The committee received Likud’s request and is reviewing it as part of this operation.” 4.07pm - Likud claims Arab parties 'stole’ election, calls for investigation into alleged fraud “The elections in Israel were stolen by Arab parties that support terror and the elimination of the Jewish state through serious criminal offenses of bribery, threats, violence, forgeries and the use of illegal software to mobilize voters,” said Prime Minister Netanyahu’s party in a statement, demanding a “thorough investigation”. The party said it would submit hundreds of pieces of evidence to the Israel Police, Shin Bet and CEC. These include allegations of envelopes containing Ra’am ballots and cash being distributed to voters and threats against polling station workers. A CEC official earlier gave an interview to Channel 12 in which they denied claims of widespread voter fraud. Netanyahu, meanwhile, made claims that Arab voters were “stealing” the election as early as the morning of polling day, but no evidence has been provided publicly. 3.31pm – Board of Deputies celebrates successful election event, featuring former JC editor The Board of Deputies and @BritainIsrael were delighted to host an evening of analysis and discussion on the Israeli election polls last night, watching democracy unfold. We were privileged to be joined by an insightful panel featuring @RachelSJohnson, @b_judah, @MelanieGarson,… pic.twitter.com/CO45X4Gb5V — Board of Deputies of British Jews (@BoardofDeputies) October 28, 2026 2.55pm – Rumours of a poor night for Shas My fellow polling nerds claim that Shas will drop to six seats, while Likud will rise to 27. A 34-year low for Shas. To put into perspective how long ago that was, the party’s chairman back then was Aryeh Deri. — Amit Segal (@AmitSegal) October 28, 2026 2.29pm – Breakdown of seats by party as it stands Approximately 85.6% of votes counted: **Seats by Party:** - Likud – 26 (-1) - Yashar – 21 (-1) - Joint List – 12 (+1) - Beyachad (Together) – 12 - The Democrats – 8 - Yisrael Beiteinu – 7 - Ra’am – 7 (+1) - United Torah Judaism – 7 - Otzma Yehudit (Jewish Power) – 7 - Shas – 7 -… — Amit Segal (@AmitSegal) October 28, 2026 1.28pm – President Herzog urges parties to avoid another set of elections “One thing must be understood, and I said this even before the elections: We must do everything possible, especially after yesterday, to avoid another round of elections,” the president said in a statement. “Therefore, I expect everyone who comes here to do so with an open mind.” 1.23pm – (Almost) final results With 85 per cent of overall votes counted – 100 per cent of normal ballots excluding so-called double envelope votes from soldiers, prisoners and diplomatic representatives – the results are as follows: Netanyahu bloc – 53 Eisenkot bloc – 48 Arab parties – 19 Double envelope votes could take until tomorrow to count and, based on recent voting trends, could slightly dilute the Arab vote, but significant changes are now unlikely. 12.10pm – Arab Joint List confirms coalition talks with opposition bloc “The Joint List wants to assist, to help replace this government, and to pave the way for an alternative government,” Ta’al chairman Ahmad Tibi told Kan. “That is why I say that we are extending a hand to what has been called the ‘change bloc,’ to help establish an alternative government and replace this terrible government.” 11.54am – Tel Aviv vs the world? If Israel were the "State of Tel Aviv", the "Change Bloc" would have won a landslide of 101 out of 120 seats. The Likud would be the only coalition party to get past the electoral threshold. Ben-Gvir, Smotrich, Haredim—all out. But Israel is not Tel Aviv. pic.twitter.com/fs3qYKGY7B — Eylon Levy (@EylonALevy) October 28, 2026 11.32am - We are ready to oust Netanyahu, says Arab Joint List Yousef Jabareen, who leads the alliance made up of three smaller Arab parties, said it is now “a decisive force in politics”. “We will be prepared to pave the way for ousting the Netanyahu, Ben-Gvir and Smotrich government and sending them home,” he went on. “The choice is between continued racism, exclusion and supremacy, or a genuine Jewish-Arab partnership.” The faction is, per the latest data, expected to win around 13 seats. In theory, this would give it significant power to decide the balance of power. However, both prospective governing blocs contain enough parties who refuse to sit with the Joint List to pose a significant challenge in forming any coalition. 11.06am – Analysis: Netanyahu is down but not out – this is no time to bet against the comeback king By JC Political Correspondent Jane Prinsley, in Israel Both sides have claimed victory. But as things stand there is no clear winner. Netanyahu is doing better than the exit polls predicted. It may not be enough to secure a majority, but it leaves those who campaigned to remove him at all costs facing uncomfortable truths about the Israeli electorate… Read the full piece here. 10.49am – How can parties lose seats? A very good question that came up at the JC offices this morning. Unlike the UK or US, Israel does not have any constituencies, so parties do not win specific seats. Instead, every party above the 3.25 per cent electoral threshold receives seats based on its proportion of the vote down to a minimum of four, so as one party's share increases, others’ can decrease and, thus, they can end up with a lower seat total compared with an earlier stage of the count. 10.44am – 84 per cent of votes now counted The latest data boosts the Eisenkot block to 49, with the Arab parties dropping to 17 9.15am – After 76 per cent of votes counted, the Likud-led bloc has 54 seats, the Eisenkot-led bloc has 47 and Arab parties have 19 Markets are not impressed with the lack of clarity. The Tel Aviv Stock Exchange’s TA-125 benchmark index slumps 1.7 per cent and the TA-35 index of blue-chip companies slips 1.5 per cent. Trump, however, sees an opportunity, claiming on Truth Social that his endorsement of Netanyahu turned around his campaign and may still carry him back to office: “When President Trump endorsed Bibi Netanyahu, the whole tide turned, and now, rather than a decisive defeat for a Great Prime Minister, it looks like a big come-from-behind stalemate, or even a WIN for Netanyahu. It all took place AFTER the Endorsement by President Trump, who… pic.twitter.com/cQwcwJB6PV — Commentary Donald J. Trump Truth Social Posts On X (@TrumpTruthOnX) October 28, 2026 8.20am – Shekel drops v dollar over inconclusive result The shekel drops against the US dollar amid uncertainty over who will lead the next government, depreciating 0.7 per cent to NIS 3.0765 per dollar in morning trading in Tel Aviv. 8.10am – After 72 per cent of votes counted, the Likud-led bloc has 54 seats, the Eisenkot-led bloc has 48 and Arab parties have 18 Yair Golan, leader of the Democrats, is urging parties in the bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot to join up with with the Arab parties and form a government. “Netanyahu lost. I know how to count to 120. 65 is more than 55. That’s how Israeli democracy works. Period,” Golan writes on X. “The reality must teach us one resounding lesson: We have no future here if we don’t stop being afraid. And if we don’t stop with the racism.” 6.40am – Advantage Netanyahu? While Netanyahu still lacks a clear path to the 61 seats needed to form a governing coalition, some Israeli analysts are suggesting – based on his 54 seats so far – he could receive the first opportunity to form Israel’s next government. 6.05am – With 50 per cent of votes counted, the pro-Netanyahu bloc has 54 seats and the anti-Netanyahu bloc 48 Another election, another inconclusive result – so far. With 50 per cent of votes counted, neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor his main rival Gadi Eisenkot are within reach of the 61 seats needed for a governing majority in the 120-seat parliament. Two key points based on results so far. First, Netanyahu’s path to staying in power is unclear. Second, the Arab parties have so far won an unprecedented 16 seats, a number which may well grow. But since two key anti-Bibi bloc leaders – Avigdor Lieberman and Naftali Bennett – have ruled out forming a government with them, Eisenkot’s path to victory is also unclear. The large number of Arab seats has almost certainly been driven by a historically high turnout, claimed by Arab parties to have been 75 per cent – amid a general-population turnout of at least 77.7 per cent, the highest since 1977. The final voter turnout among IDF soldiers reached 79.9 per cent, according to the military – an increase of 6.2 per cent compared to the previous election in 2022. Three parties are currently below the threshold of 3.25 per cent of overall votes cast needed to enter the Knesset: Reservists (2.7 per cent), People of Israel (1.7 per cent), Charedi Public (0.2 per cent). The results will change as counting continues. Since there are more questions than answers at the moment, here are some people going to vote on camels: View this post on Instagram A post shared by The Jewish Chronicle (@thejewishchronicle) 1.40am – Likud is biggest party crows Netanyahu at Jerusalem HQ Arriving shortly before 3am Israel time to speak to his supporters at the Likud election headquarters in Jerusalem, prime minster Benjamin Netanyahu appeared defiantly determined to stay on in power, despite opposition leaders telling him to quit. Appearing to claim a victory for his coalition enabling him to stay on in power, he said: “The right-wing bloc has a decisive majority.” Exit polling has suggested no bloc as any of them currently stand will be able to call on the 61 seats needed out of the total of 120 in the Knesset, but Netanyahu said: “We are still waiting for the true results,” and added: “The Likud is the biggest party in Israel.” Turning to the Islamic Republic which he long fought to weaken and ultimately vanquish, Netanyahu said: “Iran is weaker than ever, Israel is stronger than ever.” He added: “Israel is facing a historic, one-time opportunity along with our friend President Trump, to remove the Iranian threat once and for all. “We have been able to overcome our enemies, and we will be able to in the future.” The remarks come amid ongoing speculation that the US and Israel will resume attacks on Iran after the mid-term elections in America next week, following which Trump may feel less constrained by worries about his own electorate. Netanyahu also warned against a government including what he described as “antizionist” Arab parties, while hinting at being open to a wider coalition with other parties, saying: “The Zionist majority must come to its senses and unite.” However, he ruled out the possibility of compromising with coalition parties and agreeing to a “rotation” agreement allowing other leaders to be prime minister. 1.15 – … and then a set-back for Bibi In a sign of the fast-changing nature of events – and the noisy nature of exit poll updates – Channel 14 have revised the count downwards for Netanyahu’s bloc to just 60, denying him a majority. Crucially, it found that Avigdor Lieberman’s Yisrael Beytenu Party has passed the all-important 3.25 per cent threshold, allowing it pick up seats in the Knesset that otherwise might well go to Likud. 1am – Boost for Benjamin Netanyahu as count continues Although exit polls suggested there was no overall winner, as the night wore on into the early hours the position of Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party appeared to be improving. The Channel 12 exit poll adjusted its earlier figures to give the current government bloc 52 seats – up from the 50 earlier – while the opposition seats in this estimate numbered just 49, down from 52. Meanwhile, the Arab parties remained in a position of unprecedented strength, with the Arab Joint List and Ra’am together still set to claim 19 seats. In a finding that if borne out by reality would horrify the opposition, the Channel 14 updated exit poll gave a projection of 61 seats for Netanyahu’s coalition, giving a slim one-seat majority. The poll – at this stage an outlier compared with those of other outlets – found a significant game-changer in its estimate that the Yisrael Beytenu Party of Avigdor Lieberman would fail to meet the 3.25 per cent threshold of the overall vote required of all Knesset parties. The redistributed votes are likely to boost Likud’s share. Still at this very early stage late in the night, there was a further fillip for Netanyahu, with the Central Elections Committee at 2.30am Israeli time declaring that it had completed the count of the first 100,000 ballots, with 27 per cent of the vote going to Likud. For Yashar led by Gadi Eisenkot there was a share of just 17 per cent, still far ahead of the 9 per cent for the Naftali Bennett-led B’Yachad party. With the counting continuing and amid the wait for the hundreds of thousands of votes from serving soldiers, the final result is unlikely to emerge before Thursday. 12.05am – We want government replaced, says Ra’am leader Mansour Abbas, the leader of Israel’s largest Islamist party, Ra’am, has spoken of his wish to see an end to the current government. With his party projected to take around seven seats in the Knesset – as part of a wider Arab bloc totalling 17 or 18 seats – he told Channel 12: “Arab society has reacted to this government’s policy,” adding: “We want to replace it in almost every way.” As exit polls suggest neither of the two blocs – for and against Benjamin Netanyahu – may be able to form an overall majority, Abbas said: "With the numbers we have now, there is no government." The Knesset member who made history in 2021 as the first Arab-Muslim to join the cabinet as a government minister added he had been contacted by both blocs for exploratory talks on forming a coalition. 11.35pm – Yair Lapid claims: State of Israel was saved today Opposition leader and former prime minister Yair Lapid told supporters in Tel Aviv the “State of Israel was saved today” in the election, while also hinting at the possibility of forming a minority government. The former television presenter said: “The State of Israel was saved today. To be more accurate, the State of Israel saved itself today. “This country was saved today. Benjamin Netanyahu and his government collapsed today, this is a total defeat for them.” While exit polls are uncertain, with the final results unlikely to be conclusive until Thursday, he claimed for the anti-Netanyahu bloc: “We are the majority. In a democracy, the side that brings more votes – won. And it needs, it can and it is its duty to form a government.” However, Lapid appeared to recognise a majority may be not available, saying: “The mission is clear: to form a Zionist government. It may not be perfect on day one, but we will strengthen it going forward.” Opening the possibility of extensive ongoing negotiations, he added: “It may not be a broad coalition on day one, but we will expand it going forward.” Paying tribute to his political partner, Lapid said: “I also want to say to my brother, Naftali Bennett: when we brought our parties together, no one believed it would last.
